The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

Receipts not allocated to Invoices

Account used for posting product cost adjustments (e.g. landed costs)

Picking Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Picking Sequence in the locator setup, represents the Picking Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a pick list will be sorted by the picking sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine allocates products in the locator picking sequence.
The Picking Sequence in the zone setup represents the Picking Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. During product allocation for picking, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine allocates products in the zone picking sequence of static zones followed by the locator picking sequence.

The Relative Priority indicates the location to pick from first if an product is stored in more than one location. (100 = highest priority, 0 = lowest). For outgoing shipments, the location is picked with the highest priority where the entire quantity can be shipped from. If there is no location, the location with the highest priority is used. The Priority is ignored for products with Guarantee Date (always the oldest first) or if a speific instance is selected. Incoming receipts are stored at the location with the hoghest priority, if not explicitly selected.

Putaway Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Putaway Sequence in the locator setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a putaway list will be sorted by the putaway sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine will search for locators in the locator putaway sequence.
The Putaway Sequence in the zone setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. When searching for locators to putaway products, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine searches for locators in the zone putaway sequence of static zones followed by the locator putaway sequence.
The Locator indicates where in a Warehouse a product is located.

The SO Sub Type indicates the type of sales order this document refers to. This field only appears when the Document Base Type is Sales Order. The selection made here will determine which documents will be generated when an order is processed and which documents must be generated manually or in batches.
The following outlines this process.
SO Sub Type of Standard Order will generate just the Order document when the order is processed.
The Delivery Note, Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Warehouse Order will generate the Order and Delivery Note.
The Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Credit Order will generate the Order, Delivery Note and Invoice.
The Reciept must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of POS (Point of Sale) will generate all document.
The Document Copies indicates the number of copies of each document that will be generated.
The Document Type determines document sequence and processing rules

The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.
A description is limited to 255 characters.

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value} or @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@
@Name@>J
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

Data storage encryption (in Table/Column) - data is stored encrypted in the database (dangerous!) and you will not be able to report on those columns. Independent from Display encryption.

Display hashing (in Screen/Tab/Field): All characters will appear as random alphanumeric values. The actual data is stored in a hashed format in the database. These columns will not be available for reporting. Data storage hashing (in Table/Column): This is a one-way process. Once the data is hashed, it cannot be reverted to its original form.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

You can enter simple logic using variables like @Created@=@Updated@, which fires, when a record is created. If you need to evaluate also values of other records, you need to use SQL logic and need to prefix this logic with "SQL=". Example: start a Order verify workflow, when a business partner ordered something and is over the credit limit "SQL=EXISTS (SELECT * FROM C_BPartner bp WHERE C_Order. C_BPartner_ID=bp. C_BPartner_ID AND SO_CreditUsed > SO_CreditLimit)". Note that the SQL based logic checks for duplicate workflows (i.e. a workflow is started only once per record).

The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.
A description is limited to 255 characters.

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value} or @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@
@Name@>J
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)

The Cost Rollup program populates costs in this cost element for product assemblies. It sums up the material cost of all the component requirements for the product assembly and saves it in this cost element. This enables you to see to the complete cost breakup of a product assembly by viewing the costs in different cost elements for manufacturing material, material overhead, resource and overhead.

Valid options are Per Item and Per Batch. With Per Item, the quantity consumed or charged increases in proportion to the number of products being manufactured. With Per Batch, the quantity is consumed once per batch of the product being manufactured. Batch size is specified in the Product window.

Column.ColumnHelp:
The Mail Template indicates the mail template for return messages. Mail text can include variables. The priority of parsing is User/Contact, Account and then the underlying business object (like Request, Dunning, Workflow object).
So, @Name@ would resolve into the User name (if user is defined defined), then Account name (if Account is defined) and then the Name of the business object if it has a Name.
For Multi-Lingual systems, the template is translated based on the Account's language selection.

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

The Sales Volume indicates the total volume of sales for a Business Partner.

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

A search key allows you a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).
The type of product also determines accounting consequences.
The Created On field indicates the date that this record was created.
The Updated field indicates the date that this record was updated.
The Created By field indicates the user who created this record.
The Updated By field indicates the user who updated this record.
A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients. Tenant is a synonym for Client.

ValidationRule.ValidationCode: AD_Client.AD_Client_ID <> 0

Column.ColumnHelp: An organization is a unit of your Tenant or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

ValidationRule.ValidationCode: (AD_Org.IsSummary='N' OR AD_Org.AD_Org_ID=0) AND AD_Org.IsCostCenter='N' AND AD_Org.IsProfitCenter='N'
ValidationRule.Description: Not Summary - 0 - Organizations of the Client with user acces rights

Column.ColumnHelp: An Accounting Schema defines the rules used in accounting such as costing method, currency and calendar
Indicates the Currency to be used when processing or reporting on this record
You can define multiple cost types. A cost type selected in an Accounting Schema is used for accounting.
Identifies the category which this product belongs to. Product categories are used for pricing and selection.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
The Bill of Materials check box indicates if this product consists of a bill of materials.
Identifies an item which is either purchased or sold in this organization.
